newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks ends bourse lower, picks up in IBIS.
newsitem.headline: German stocks ends bourse lower, picks up in IBIS.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade down on Monday as floor dealings caught up with losses made during late Friday electronic dealings and weaker German bonds weighed on the market.

The DAX index of 30 leading shares ended down 11.39 points, or 0.42 percent, down at 2,671.86 matching a fall on Friday afternoon on the IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computer trade in the DAX index.

But on Monday, despite a slightly weaker opening on Wall Street, the IBIS DAX moved ahead in post-bourse dealings, to end up 8.54 points, or 0.32 percent, at 2,678.73 points, encouraged by a recovery in German bonds.
Dealers said they saw the DAX index making no dramatic moves ahead of the U.S. elections on Tuesday, but said it was also well-supported around current levels.
Although the U.S. election will be the week's main focus, a flurry of German data and company results was also likely to keep the market entertained.

DAX companies, chemicals firm Bayer AG and Commerzbank are due to release nine month results on Tuesday, followed by chemical company Hoechst AG on Wednesday and car maker Daimler on Thursday. All four were amongst the most heavily traded companies of the day.
Daimler shares, which were popular last week, continued to rise, gaining 70 pfennigs to end IBIS trade at 90.60 marks.
Shares in car maker Volkswagen also benefited from interest in the auto industry, rising 5.40 marks to 616.70 marks.
The day's main market-moving news was the confirmation over the weekend of the merger between British Telecommunications Plc and U.S firm MCI Communications.
German mixed utility Viag AG, BT's partner in Germany, climbed over one percent, or seven marks to 568.90 marks in IBIS trade.
Amongst the medium-capitalised firms, SGL Carbon shares fell after the company's third quarter operating profit came in slightly weaker than expected, up 4.4 percent on last year at 71 million marks.
Shares in the company, the world's largest carbon and graphite maker, were down two marks at 170.00 marks in IBIS dealings.
